But every figure came through secondary coverage and search snippets; no primary 10-Q/10-K was opened.

cluster_thesis.text: Demand has not rolled. Azure grew +43% and guides ~45% for the next quarter, Google Cloud +82% with a $514B backlog, AWS +37%, and wave-1 verified 2026 capex unchanged after the Amodei essay. I moved innings from 'rolling' to 'late' because 'rolling' implies demand deterioration, which the evidence contradicts. The late-cycle signature is funding. Among US hyperscalers only MSFT still generates positive FCF: GOOG posted its first negative-FCF quarter and AMZN's TTM FCF is -$7.6B, and GOOG says 2027 capex rises significantly again. So the cluster is becoming externally funded just as the 10-yr is +32bp/1m and a hike is ~84-92% priced for 09-16. Status stays watch. The tailwind is intact, but the cost of the capital funding it is rising, and the market will pay less per unit of growth.
cluster_thesis.falsifier: Watch breaks toward 'deteriorating' if any of MSFT/GOOG/AMZN guides 2027 capex flat-to-down, or if cloud growth decelerates (Azure <40%, Google Cloud <50%, AWS <33%) while capex still rises, in the 10-28..10-30 prints. It breaks toward 'intact' if GOOG and AMZN FCF turn back positive in Q3 with growth held.

margin_pool.moving_toward: Capacity owners that sell their own demand at the highest growth per capex dollar and still self-fund: MSFT on funding, GOOG on growth and backlog (TPU plus $514B backlog). Short-term, also toward neocloud landlords renting bridge capacity to hyperscalers, and toward component and memory vendors whose pricing is inflating hyperscaler capex.
margin_pool.moving_away_from: Hyperscaler owners' cash margin generally: capex is now partly price rather than volume ('higher component pricing' at MSFT, memory cost at AMZN). Specifically away from AMZN, which has the slowest cloud growth against the largest capex guide, and from floating-rate or convert-funded neocloud equity, where a hike reprices funding cost directly.

Alphabet Q2 OCF $39.07B minus capex $44.92B = FCF -$5.855B, its first negative FCF quarter
Azure +43%, >$100B annual revenue, next quarter guided ~45% cc; Q4 capex $41B including higher component pricing; Q4 FCF $19.6B; CY26 capex ~$175B after a finance-to-operating-lease shift

Its OpenAI-linked commitments are the least disclosed. It has the lowest ATR (2.0%), so it captures the least upside in a snap-back. Its rank agrees with price, and the agreement rests on FCF and Azure acceleration, not on the +6.5pp rel_intra.

GOOG Q3 (2026-10-29): Cloud growth >=60% AND FCF back positive -> GOOG takes rank 1 if MSFT's Azure is <43%; Cloud growth <50% with FCF negative a second quarter -> GOOG falls to 3 behind AMZN
AMZN Q3 (2026-10-30): AWS >=40% with TTM FCF improving toward zero -> AMZN passes GOOG; AWS <33% -> AMZN gap to rank 2 widens

redundant_pairs.same_bet_because: Screen candidate only (1m return gap 1.21pp, ATR gap 0.04). On business grounds they are distinct. MSFT is enterprise software/Copilot plus OpenAI-linked Azure and still self-funds; GOOG is ad-funded, has a mature TPU and the fastest cloud share gain, and is now FCF-negative. They share enterprise cloud customers, but their accelerator strategy, funding state and end-market mix differ. The near-identical price action comes from the same 'quality mega-cap in a semis selloff' factor, not the same business bet.
Partial overlap: MSFT is an NBIS customer, so part of NBIS revenue is MSFT capex rented out. NBIS layers a financing and rate factor MSFT lacks. Carried from 09-14 and unchanged.

thesis_tensions.tension: The rank agrees, but the evidence doesn't back 'strengthening' cleanly. The thesis is marked unverified and was status-only trimmed. This run found GOOG's first negative-FCF quarter (-$5.855B) and guidance for a significantly larger 2027 capex, a material evidence_against the thesis does not carry. It also contradicts the FactSet FCF-positive claim the 09-14 ladder carried.
Agrees on rank. The thesis lacks the 15->25yr useful-life change and the finance-to-operating-lease shift, an earnings-quality evidence_against that flatters reported capex.

The 09-14 swap of AMZN above GOOG was wrong on evidence: GOOG's growth axis was evidenceable (Cloud +82%) and it had led AMZN by ~4.9pp rel_intra. That swap is reversed here.

Mis-clustering flag: NBIS is a capacity SELLER funded by credit, not a capacity buyer. Its ATR (7.5%) is ~3.5x the majors'. Using weight x ATR20 as a rough risk proxy (not a correlation), NBIS is ~54% of this cluster's risk at 3.2% weight (NBIS 24.2 of ~44.6 total). The 'cluster below 15% target / $3,800 room' figure mixes two different risk factors. Suggest a Neocloud sub-cluster (NBIS, CRWV, IREN) or a financing-risk tag in the playbook.
Q3 useful-life/lease changes at GOOG/AMZN not checked.
